To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we determined the crystal structure of a fungal sterol carrier protein, which has potential applications as a fungicidal agent.

we have crystallized oligandrin, the sterol-carrier protein from the fungus Pythium oligandum, in the space group C222, with cell dimensions of a= 94.0 b= 171.1 c= 55.3 and four molecules per asymmetric unit.
we have crystallized oligandrin and a cholesterol-oligandrin complex and that these crystals diffract to a high resolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of oligandrin and its interaction with cholesterol.
the development of novel, non-toxic and non-antibiotic, biological control strategies against phytopathogenic fungi.
the study of a protein with potential applications in the field of biotechnology, and we have obtained crystals suitable for high-resolution structure determination by X-ray diffraction methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data collected from the free and complexed forms of the protein have been processed to a resolution of 2.0 and 1.85 A, respectively.
this study has provided the first structural data on an alpha-elicitin, and the results obtained will allow the design of new strategies to improve the biological activity of oligandrin.

the crystallographic structure determination of this complex has provided the most detailed structural information available on the molecular interactions between a fungal elicitor and its target lipid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to crystallize oligandrin and its cholesterol complex.
we have obtained crystals of oligandrin that diffract to 2.4 A resolution.
oligandrin is a protein with a novel fold and that the cholesterol complex is the first example of a lipid-carrier protein with a known structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oligandrin is a sterol carrier and that its structure can be solved by X-ray crystallography.
the use of a lipid complex in the crystallization conditions can be used to improve the quality of protein crystals.
it is possible to crystallize and study a protein complexed with cholesterol, a small molecule, at high resolution.
